full_text_en:
China Merchants Bank Co., Ltd. Dalian Branch v. Dalian Yifang Real Estate Co., Ltd.
— Guarantee Contract Dispute

Ruling Summary

Phased guarantee is relatively common in pre-sale commercial housing contracts. By registering a preliminary mortgage on the purchased property of the buyer, the risks of financial institutions and real estate enterprises can be effectively reduced. Because of its phased nature, the connection between preliminary mortgage registration and pre-sale commercial housing registration is very important. A financial institution's neglect in handling preliminary mortgage registration effectively extends the guarantee period of the real estate enterprise indefinitely, which violates the spirit of the guarantee law and also the principle of good faith.

Civil Ruling of the Supreme People's Court
(2017) Supreme People's Court Civil Application No. 3474

Re-applicant (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): China Merchants Bank Co., Ltd. Dalian Branch. Address: Part of Floors 1-3, BOC Tower, No. 17 Renmin Road, Zhongshan District, Dalian City, Liaoning Province.
Responsible Person: Qian Xi, Branch Manager.
Agent Ad Litem: Shang Qingguo, lawyer of Liaoning Xianhe Law Firm.
Agent Ad Litem: Bi Shumin, lawyer of Liaoning Xianhe Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Dalian Yifang Real Estate Co., Ltd. Address: No. 7, Zone C1, Xinghai Square, Shahekou District, Dalian City, Liaoning Province.
Legal Representative: Sun Xishuang, Chairman of the Company.
Agent Ad Litem: Zhang Guohan, lawyer of Liaoning Zhiku Law Firm.
Agent Ad Litem: Bai Yulong, lawyer of Liaoning Zhiku Law Firm.

The re-applicant, China Merchants Bank Co., Ltd. Dalian Branch (hereinafter referred to as China Merchants Bank), disagreeing with the civil judgment (2017) Liao Min Zhong No. 156 rendered by the Liaoning High People's Court in the case of the guarantee contract dispute with the respondent, Dalian Yifang Real Estate Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Yifang Company), applied to this Court for a retrial. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law to review this case, which has now concluded.

China Merchants Bank applied for a retrial, stating: 1. The judgment of the second instance found that China Merchants Bank did not assert its rights against Yifang Company within the guarantee period, that the guarantee period had expired, and that Yifang Company's guarantee liability should be discharged. This finding was based on unclear facts, and the application of Article 26(2) of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter the Guarantee Law) to determine that Yifang Company's guarantee liability should be discharged constituted an error in the application of the law. 2. The judgment of the second instance found that China Merchants Bank was negligent in handling the preliminary mortgage registration, which led to the mortgaged property being sealed up by the court, and that it should bear the legal consequences itself. This finding was an error in the determination of facts. 3. The judgment of the second instance found that the responsibility for not handling the preliminary mortgage registration for the property in question lay with China Merchants Bank. This was an error in the determination of facts. 4. The judgment of the second instance used a presumption method to conclude that because the preliminary mortgage registration for the property in question was not handled, and the possibility of reasons other than the bank's fault could not be excluded, the responsibility was directly attributed to China Merchants Bank. This principle of imputation contradicts the guarantee contract agreement and is also inconsistent with legal provisions. Requests: 1. Revoke the civil judgment (2017) Liao Min Zhong No. 156 of the Liaoning High People's Court. 2. Retry this case, or instruct the Liaoning High People's Court to retry this case, and amend the judgment to support the claims of China Merchants Bank. China Merchants Bank applied for a retrial pursuant to Items (2) and (6) of Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.

Yifang Company submitted its opinion, stating: 1. The guarantee in question was a "phased guarantee." According to the agreement of both parties and the law, the guarantee period should end on the date when, after Yifang Company delivered the registration and filing documents for the property purchase contract, China Merchants Bank completed the preliminary mortgage registration within a reasonable period. 2. According to the contract, Yifang Company's obligation was only to deliver the registration and filing documents for the property purchase contract to China Merchants Bank. Since Yifang Company had fulfilled its obligation, China Merchants Bank, as the party responsible for handling the preliminary mortgage registration, should bear the liability for failing to do so. 3. When Yifang Company transferred the filing contract for the property in question to China Merchants Bank, the property was already eligible for property rights registration and mortgage registration, and there was no need for preliminary mortgage registration. 4. The evidence of China Merchants Bank had sufficiently proven that when handling the loan business in question, it was processed as "commercial property purchase loan," not "personal housing loan." According to the Guarantee Agreement, the loan in question did not fall within the scope of guaranteed debt for "personal housing loan" as defined in the Guarantee Agreement, and Yifang Company should not bear any guarantee liability for the loan in question. In summary, the retrial application of China Merchants Bank lacked factual and legal basis, and it requested dismissal.

This Court is of the opinion that the focal issue of dispute in this case is: whether Yifang Company should bear guarantee liability.

The Individual Housing Purchase Loan and Guarantee Contract signed between China Merchants Bank and Gao Zhi, and the Guarantee Agreement signed between China Merchants Bank and Yifang Company, are both true expressions of the parties' intentions, do not violate the mandatory provisions of laws and administrative regulations, and should be deemed legal and valid.

Regarding the determination of the guarantee period in this case. Article 5 of the Guarantee Agreement between China Merchants Bank and Yifang Company stipulates that Yifang Company provides a phased guarantee, with the guarantee period commencing from the date of disbursement of each loan and ending on the date of completion of the preliminary mortgage registration. The purpose of the Guarantee Agreement signed by the parties was for Yifang Company to complete the preliminary mortgage registration procedures for the property purchased by Gao Zhi within 90 working days and deliver them to China Merchants Bank. After China Merchants Bank completed the preliminary mortgage registration, Yifang Company's guarantee liability could be discharged, and China Merchants Bank would secure the realization of its claims through the mortgage right. Literally, the parties agreed on a guarantee period, with the completion of preliminary mortgage registration as the time point, and the guarantee period could be extended or shortened. This agreement was the true intention of both parties, but it could not contravene the provisions of the Guarantee Law, nor could it extend the guarantee period indefinitely, which is also an inherent meaning of a phased guarantee. Therefore, the guarantee period in this case should be determined as from October 9, 2012, when China Merchants Bank disbursed the loan, to the date when, after Yifang Company delivered the preliminary mortgage registration documents for the commercial property to China Merchants Bank on January 17, 2014, China Merchants Bank completed the preliminary mortgage registration within a reasonable period. Article 7 of the Guarantee Agreement stipulates that if, for reasons not attributable to China Merchants Bank, the preliminary mortgage registration for the property purchased by the borrower cannot be completed within 90 working days, China Merchants Bank has the right to require Yifang Company to perform the guarantee liability from the date of loan disbursement until the date of completion of the preliminary mortgage registration. Similarly, after Yifang Company delivers the registration and filing documents of the property purchase contract to China Merchants Bank, China Merchants Bank should also handle the preliminary mortgage registration within a reasonable period, and the reasonable period should refer to the above-stated 90 working days agreed upon by both parties.

Regarding the responsibility for not handling the preliminary mortgage registration for the property in question. Article 6 of the Guarantee Agreement stipulates that during the period of assuming the guarantee, Yifang Company shall handle the true and valid registration and filing procedures for the property purchase contract, promptly transfer the registration and filing documents of the property purchase contract to the designated agency of China Merchants Bank, and actively cooperate with China Merchants Bank in handling the preliminary mortgage registration. In the first instance, China Merchants Bank argued that the reason for not handling the preliminary mortgage registration was the lack of cooperation from Gao Zhi. Because Gao Zhi was a Hong Kong resident, it was difficult to contact him, and he did not provide the agency procedures, so the bank could not unilaterally handle the registration. Article 26.2 of the Individual Housing Purchase Loan and Guarantee Contract signed between China Merchants Bank and Gao Zhi stipulates: "If the mortgaged property has not obtained the title certificate at the time of signing this contract, the mortgagor shall, at the request of the lender, actively cooperate with the lender and/or the seller to handle the preliminary mortgage registration or floor mortgage registration; within 60 days after the mortgaged property meets the conditions for formal mortgage registration, the mortgagor must unconditionally cooperate with the lender to complete the procedures for converting the preliminary mortgage registration or floor mortgage registration into formal mortgage registration." In the first and second instances, China Merchants Bank did not provide evidence to prove that the failure to handle the preliminary mortgage registration was caused by Yifang Company's delay in delivering the documents for handling the preliminary mortgage registration, nor did it provide evidence that it had actively urged Yifang Company and Gao Zhi to cooperate in handling the preliminary mortgage registration. After receiving the preliminary mortgage registration documents delivered by Yifang Company on January 17, 2014, China Merchants Bank did not promptly handle the preliminary mortgage registration within a reasonable period. It was not until March 6, 2015, when the property in question was sealed up by the court in another case and could not be registered, that China Merchants Bank sued Yifang Company in court on April 22, 2015, to assert its rights. China Merchants Bank was obviously negligent in performing its contractual obligations and was significantly at fault for the consequence of being unable to handle the preliminary mortgage registration for the property in question.

Regarding whether Yifang Company should bear guarantee liability. In this case, China Merchants Bank was the party obligated to handle the preliminary mortgage registration. Where Yifang Company had not delivered the documents for handling the preliminary mortgage registration within the agreed 90 working days, after receiving the delayed documents from Yifang Company, China Merchants Bank should have promptly handled the preliminary mortgage registration within a reasonable period to prevent the property in question from being sealed up by the court and becoming unregisterable. However, after receiving the delayed preliminary mortgage registration documents from Yifang Company, China Merchants Bank not only raised no objection but also failed to handle the preliminary mortgage registration for over a year without a reasonable explanation. This should be deemed as the fulfillment of the condition for the discharge of Yifang Company's phased guarantee liability. According to Article 26(2) of the Guarantee Law, which provides: "If, within the guarantee period agreed in the contract and the guarantee period prescribed in the preceding paragraph, the creditor does not demand that the guarantor bear the guarantee liability, the guarantor shall be discharged from the guarantee liability," China Merchants Bank did not assert its rights against Yifang Company within the guarantee period, and Yifang Company's guarantee liability is discharged. Furthermore, Article 119(1) of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "After one party breaches the contract, the other party shall take appropriate measures to prevent the loss from expanding; if the loss is expanded due to the failure to take appropriate measures, the other party shall not claim compensation for the expanded loss." Therefore, the responsibility for the consequence that the mortgaged property was sealed up by the court due to China Merchants Bank's neglect in performing its obligation to handle the preliminary mortgage registration should be borne by China Merchants Bank itself.

Given that Yifang Company's guarantee liability has been discharged, whether Gao Zhi's loan falls within the scope of the guarantee in this case no longer needs to be examined, and this Court will not review it.

In summary, the retrial application of China Merchants Bank does not meet the circumstances specified in Items (2) and (6) of Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. Pursuant to Article 204(1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 395(2) of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, it is ruled as follows:

The retrial application of China Merchants Bank Co., Ltd. Dalian Branch is dismissed.

Presiding Judge: Wu Jianhua
Judge: Dong Hua
Judge: Zhang Nengbao

September 26, 2017

Judge Assistant: Ma Hening
